headline: Senators place Linus Ullmark on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Senators have placed goalie Linus Ullmark on injured reserve after he left their 5-1 win over the Panthers with a lower-body injury.

The timing stings for Ottawa, because Ullmark has been a big reason for their 7-3-0 start. He has a .945 save percentage in eight games so far this season, and goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie has stopped compared with what an average goalie would have allowed on the same shots, sits at 8.24. Last season that figure was -13.3 over 49 games, so this is a sharp turnaround, even if the sample is still small. The team numbers show how much he matters: OTT's goalies have saved 2.9 goals above expected so far this season, while the team holds just 51.2 percent of expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and only 50 percent at five-on-five. Ottawa is winning more on goaltending than on territory, so losing its best-performing goalie hurts more than the record suggests. For fantasy owners, Ullmark is a hold only if your league has an injured reserve slot, and Ottawa's other goalies will face a steeper climb. The data doesn't say who covers his minutes, so check who gets the next start.
